passages.original: Ethan regio est inter Ægyptum et solitudinem in qua est Petra oppidum, in cujus spelunca habitavit Samson cum ab Allophylis infestaretur : Ei sedit, inquit, in apelunca Petrce Ethan, qui locus erat valde munitus, ut testatur Josephus ( Lib. Antiq. cap 10). Eral aulem hæc regio in principio solitudinis. Ideo dicit: Et est pars deserti. Regionis hujus meminit David propheta dicens : Tu siccatti fluvios Ethan (Psal. LXXIII , i5). In hac mansione primum apparuit Dominus nocte in columna ignis, et die in columna nubis, ostendens iter populo, ad terram usque successionis corum : Etnon defecit, innuit, columna nubis in die, et columna ignit in nocte, coram omni populo (Exod.
passages.english: Ethan is a region between Egypt and the wilderness, in which is the town of Petra, in whose cave Samson lived when he was being harassed by the Philistines: "And he sat," it says, "in the cave of the rock of Ethan," a place which was very strongly fortified, as Josephus testifies (Antiquities, book [...], ch. 10). Now this region was at the beginning of the wilderness. Therefore it says: "And it is part of the desert." David the prophet mentions this region, saying: "You dried up the rivers of Ethan" (Ps. 73:15). At this station the Lord first appeared by night in a pillar of fire and by day in a pillar of cloud, showing the way to the people as far as the land of their inheritance: "And there did not fail," it says, "the pillar of cloud by day and the pillar of fire by night, before all the people" (Exod.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: apelunca/Petrce = spelunca Petrae; Eral aulem = Erat autem; siccatti = siccasti; corum = eorum; Etnon defecit, innuit = Et non defecit, inquit; ignit = ignis. "Allophyli" ("foreigners") is the Septuagint/Vulgate term for the Philistines. The book number of Josephus is missing in the reference. "Terram successionis" taken as "land of inheritance". The scripture reference is completed in the following context (13:21).

passages.original: ideo infra subjungitur : De deserto Sin , hæc eat Cades ( Num. xx , 1). Et alibi, dum populus in hac moraretur mansione, mittens nuntios Moyses ad regem Edom : Et nunc sumus, inquit, in Cades civitate, ex parte finium tuorum (Ibid., 14). Hanc meminit David propheta , dicens : Et commovebit Dominus desertum Cades (Psal. XlVIII, 8). Hic Maria Moysi soror diem suum obivit, mortua et sepulta est, ut supra legitur. Quod Josephus quoque describit dicens : Tunc itaque sororem ejus Mariam finis vitæ accepit , [cum quadragesimum complesset annum, ex quo Ægyptum dereliquit: sepelieruntque eam publice nimis splendide (Lib. iv Antiqq. cap. 4). Hic denique penuria aquæ laborat populus; quare iratus tumultuatur in Moysen : a quo petra jussu Dei mirabili virga percussa , aqua manavit copiosa; unde bibentibus cunctis cupiditas sitis ablata est.
passages.english: Therefore below it is added: "From the desert of Sin, this is Cades" (Num. 20:1). And elsewhere, while the people were staying at this station, Moses, sending messengers to the king of Edom, says: "And now we are in Cades, a city on the edge of your borders" (ibid., 14). David the prophet mentions it, saying: "And the Lord will shake the desert of Cades" (Ps. 28:8). Here Mary, the sister of Moses, reached her last day; she died and was buried, as is read above. Josephus too describes this, saying: "At that time, then, the end of life overtook his sister Mary, when she had completed the fortieth year since she left Egypt; and they buried her publicly, with great splendour" (Antiquities, book 4, ch. 4). Here, finally, the people suffer from a lack of water, and so in anger they riot against Moses; by him, at God's command, the rock was struck with the wonderful rod, and water flowed in abundance, so that the craving of thirst was taken away from all who drank.
passages.notes: "eat" read as "est". The psalm reference "XlVIII" is evidently garbled; the verse is Ps. 28:8 (Vulgate numbering). The edition's opening bracket before "cum quadragesimum" is not closed. Mary = Miriam.
